item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukraine deployed a drone to airlift a wounded soldier from the front line, a first-of-its-kind operation. Russian drones killed children and an infant in a park in Kharkiv Oblast. The US delayed delivery of Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine, and Trump signed an executive order waiving a new Russia sanctions package, prompting Zelenskyy to accuse him of rewarding Putin. 75,767 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli police have detained ten settlers suspected of attacking a US photographer, a French mayor and other civilians in the West Bank, torching cars and olive trees and wounding farmers. The World Food Programme is ending food aid for half a million people in Gaza because of funding shortfalls, while UNICEF reports that 340 children have been killed despite a ceasefire. Israel is resuming entry of private-sector goods into Gaza, where five people have been reported killed. The conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Syria: the situation
item.description:
Israeli forces arrested two Syrian men after an incursion into Jubata al-Khashab in Quneitra, while Damascus courts continued trials of three defendants in transitional justice cases. In the north, a former Hurras al-Din commander was arrested in Idlib and the Syrian Kurdish community expressed a preference for Bashar al-Assad over Erdogan. The Syrian defense universities limited women’s admission to most programs, and the YPJ reiterated its role as a security guarantee amid an integration process. Damascus and Syrian officials warned that Druze groups, allegedly backed by Israel, may launch an offensive in Sweida. The UCDP recorded 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
Iraq is coping with security gaps after the complete US troop withdrawal as Baghdad and Tehran activate joint security committees and discuss stronger ties. Iran-backed Iraqi militias have pledged to defend Iran if attacked, while Iraqi authorities are pursuing legal action against media incitement supporting pro-Iran armed groups and have arrested a lawyer who brandished a gun in court. The Shingal mayoral post, vacant for nine years, is now open for nominations, and Jordan's king reaffirmed support for regional sovereignty and security. The conflict recorded 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: South Sudan: the situation
item.description:
Sudanese armed forces carried out a drone strike on Abyei’s Amiet market, killing dozens and injuring many, prompting South Sudan to summon Sudan’s envoy over the attack. A separate drone strike in the disputed Sudan-South Sudan border region also caused high casualties. In Ruweng, fresh attacks left nine dead and six wounded, while in Northern Bahr el Ghazal bodies arrived from Khor Kaltan killings. Communal clashes continued, including 14 deaths between Warrap and Lakes communities and a traditional chief’s arrest over a Juba youth killing. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Fitgharan forces now hold the Mogadishu-Baidoa corridor while Laftagareen forces have seized Buurhakaba and another town in the Bay region, expanding fighting in southern Somalia. Al Shabaab detonated an IED in Mandera, injuring six civilians, and the ICRC treated 148 wounded after heavy combat in Baidoa. Ethiopia announced the withdrawal of more than 3,000 troops from Somalia as its own civil war intensifies, and Ethiopia has refused to intervene in the South West State conflict. Somaliland and Puntland were designated as "friendly" in an Israeli security framework, and Somalia is screening travelers after Kenya confirmed an imported Ebola case and has agreed to acquire Pakistani JF‑17 fighter jets. The UCDP recorded 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: The Sahel insurgency: the situation
item.description:
Malian forces and their Russian allies are carrying out indiscriminate drone strikes that have killed 94 civilians, while the Malian army and rebel groups continue to abuse civilians. In Nigeria, gunmen attacked a convoy in Borno, killing 15 soldiers and task force members, and terrorists killed soldiers at a Borno military post. Bandits raided two communities in Niger, causing scores of deaths. Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso have resumed talks with ECOWAS after a withdrawal, indicating diplomatic engagement alongside the violence. The conflict caused 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:
Recent attacks include gunmen killing 15 soldiers in a convoy in Borno and a bomb explosion on a Borno road that killed nine soldiers, while bandits killed three policemen in Zamfara. In Benue, police rescued an abducted Catholic priest and seven others, and in Plateau gunmen attacked herders, killing two and injuring six, with reports of house burnings targeting Fulani communities. Islamist jihadists burned an evangelist alive in Adamawa and kidnapped a Catholic priest in Benue, also striking bases. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Iran shipped some LPG and jet fuel despite a blockade, and the Arakan Army seized over 20 soldiers' bodies and weapons in clashes near the Rakhine-Ayeyarwady border. King Charles sent books and letters to detained Aung San Suu Kyi, which the Myanmar government acknowledged. The conflict caused 2,332 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt: the situation
item.description:
Militant attacks continue in Manipur, with villagers shot while collecting firewood and a pre-dawn arson that gutted a hamlet, prompting security forces to boost operations and a statewide manhunt. Protesters have placed bodies of killed civilians outside the chief minister's residence, while the Joint Tribes Council has called for a security review after the attacks. In northern Kashmir, the Northern Army commander reviewed security and operational preparedness, and buses bound for Kashmir were attacked in Punjab and Haryana, with passengers labeled as terrorists. A cabinet expansion is planned after the lieutenant governor returns to the region. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Vice Admiral Rommel Supangan assumed command of the Philippine Coast Guard and led a rescue of four people, including a child, on Hagonoy Island, Surigao del Sur. Chinese coast guard and navy vessels entered waters near the Pratas Islands and Scarborough Shoal, while Taiwan’s coast guard and maritime forces repelled sixteen mainland Chinese ships in a coordinated operation. The United States and the Philippines conducted their sixteenth bilateral maritime exercise in the West Philippine Sea, and there were 176 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Southern Thailand: the situation
item.description:

Cambodia and Thailand agreed on confidence-building measures at a UNCLOS meeting and discussed easing maritime border tensions, while the WTO and multilateral partners reviewed progress on a supply-chain finance initiative. item.description:
The Sudanese army and Rapid Support Forces are intensifying drone strikes on civilian sites, including a livestock market in Khartoum, a market where 80 people were killed, and gold-mining areas in West Kordofan and near the Egypt border, causing dozens of civilian deaths. Recent attacks have also hit a market in southern Sudan and an artisanal gold mine in South Kordofan, killing children and many civilians. These strikes expand the use of drones from combatant targets to economic and civilian locations, increasing civilian casualties. The conflict remains between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces. 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
